hero.title: SQL Heist
hero.tagline: Every system has a door somebody forgot to lock.
hero.lede: You find them. A real database is on the other side — no simulation, no safety net but the sandbox. Pull three cases. Then learn how they should have stopped you.

what.title: Learn the break-in to learn the lock
what.lede: SQL Heist is an educational SQL-injection game. You pull the attack against a real database, then study the code that should have stopped you — offence teaches defence better than any lecture.

0.v: The practice database and every payload run in your browser; account sync is separate and optional.

1.v: A real SQLite engine, seeded fresh for every single run.

2.v: No real target — the only thing you can break is the sandbox.

what.safe: Safe by design — no account needed, no downloads, no setup.

how.title: Five moves, every time
how.lede: Every job runs the same arc, so you always know exactly where you are in it.

closer.fixerLine: “Three cases. You keep what you learn — Meridian keeps the bill.”
closer.title: The door is open. Walk through it.

0.title: Brief
0.body: Neo names the mark and the take — never the method. He points at the door; you work out the lock.

1.title: Recon
1.body: Case the target's front. Find where your input actually lands. The schema you're shown is never the whole building.

2.title: Exploit
2.body: The heart of it. Type into the mark's form and watch the real query your input builds — live, on the wire — then run it.

3.title: Loot
3.body: The take, your score, and how clean you were. Nobody stopped you. That is the whole point.

4.title: Debrief
4.body: The other side of the job: the vulnerable code beside the fix that closes it. This is the part that makes you dangerous on defence.

wire.intro: The Exploit screen shows two faces of the same moment. On the left, the ordinary form the victim sees. On the right, the raw SQL your input becomes. Colour carries meaning — and it never rides on colour alone:

0.rest: is your input, read as code — the break-out, the moment data stops being data.

1.rest: is the query's own keywords — the structure the system wrote.

2.rest: is what your comment killed. If it's grey, it never ran.

reset.name: Reset
reset.text: wipes your input and reseeds the database. Every run starts clean anyway.

stuck.body: Every job carries three hints, opened in order: a word, then the method, then the play. They cost score, so spend them like they're yours. Guessing blind is for amateurs and dead men — but a nudge beats staring.

point.body: This isn't a game about pulling off crimes. It's a game about seeing the one flaw that makes them possible — so you recognise it in the wild and shut it. You learn the break-in so you can build the lock.

faq.title: Questions Neo answers once
faq.lead: No small talk. Here's what people ask before their first job.

0.a: Yes. Every job targets only the sandboxed SQLite database in your browser. The practice payload never reaches a real system; site delivery and optional account sync are separate from the target.

1.q: Do I need to install anything?
1.a: No. It runs in a modern browser. The database engine (SQLite compiled to WebAssembly) loads on demand the first time you need it — no account needed, no downloads, no setup.

2.q: Do I need to know SQL already?
2.a: It helps. The game assumes you can read a SELECT and roughly follow a WHERE clause. It teaches you injection — not SQL from zero. If queries are brand new to you, learn the basics first, then come pull a job.

3.q: Are you teaching people to attack real websites?
3.a: We teach how injection works so you can recognise it and close it — every job ends with the fix, not the break-in. Use what you learn only on systems you own or have explicit permission to test. Anywhere else is a crime, and that's on you.

4.a: On this device, in your browser's local storage. Anonymous play uses no account and no server, so we never see it — sign in and your progress also syncs to your account. Clear your browser data, or open the game somewhere else, and local play starts fresh.

6.q: The engine won’t load, or something looks broken.
6.a: Refresh first. If it still won't start, your browser may be blocking WebAssembly or running in a locked-down mode — try a current version of Chrome, Firefox, or Safari with default settings.

7.q: Can I play in my language?
7.a: English, Turkish, and Polish. Use the language switch in the nav — the whole site and game chrome follow.

consent.title: This game uses local storage
consent.body: SQL Heist uses local storage for language, progress, this notice, and the signed-in session. A pending signup email expires after one hour and is removed the next time the app loads or checks it; clearing site data removes it sooner. No analytics or advertising tracking. Account sync uses Supabase; public profiles require explicit opt-in.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Anonymous by default. Optional accounts sync only the data needed for your identity, progress, and chosen public presence.
privacy.glanceBody: You can play without an account: gameplay and progress stay in local storage, while the host still receives the normal request needed to serve the site. An optional account sends the account and progress data described below to Supabase. No analytics or advertising trackers are included in this build.

0.title: Controller and contact
0.body: We operate SQL Heist and act as the data controller for the processing described in this notice. Privacy and data-rights requests can be sent to melih.sarac@hotmail.com.

1.title: Data we process
1.body: Data is collected electronically: directly from the signup/profile forms and your browser, through Supabase API requests when signed in, and automatically through ordinary hosting requests. Anonymous play does not require a name or email. Your browser stores your language choice and completed case objectives locally; hosting requests may include IP address, user agent, requested URL, and time.
1.body2: If you create an account, we process your email, chosen username, optional display name, public-profile choice and consent history (grant or withdrawal, notice version, source, and time), completed case and objective identifiers, and account/progress timestamps. Your password goes directly to Supabase Auth; only a salted password hash is retained, and the operator cannot read the password. If you email us, we also process your address, message contents, sent/received times, and ordinary mail-routing metadata. We do not send your SQL practice payloads to Supabase or intentionally collect special-category data.

2.title: Local and synced progress
2.body: Progress is always written to your browser first. While signed in, completed-objective sets are also merged into your account so progress can move across devices without deleting either copy. Clearing browser data removes the local copy, not the account copy; signing out does not erase either. Account settings let you export or request deletion of the synced copy.

3.title: Purposes and legal bases
3.body: We process account identity, authentication, export, deletion requests, and cross-device progress to provide the optional account service you request (GDPR Article 6(1)(b); KVKK Article 5(2)(c)). Browser storage needed for language, local progress, and an authenticated session is used to deliver those requested features.
3.body2: Publishing a profile or leaderboard entry relies on your explicit, revocable choice (GDPR Article 6(1)(a); KVKK explicit consent). Limited hosting and security logs may be processed to operate and protect the service (GDPR Article 6(1)(f); KVKK Article 5(2)(f)). Correspondence is processed to answer support or rights requests and keep required evidence (GDPR Articles 6(1)(b), (c), and (f), as applicable; KVKK Article 5(2)(c), (ç), and (f)). We do not sell data, use it for advertising, or make decisions about you solely by automated means.

4.title: Public profile and casual leaderboard
4.body: Accounts are private by default. If you opt in, your username, optional display name, join date, objectives-cleared count, and activity timestamp may appear publicly. Email and internal user ID are never included. You can withdraw the opt-in from account settings; the profile and leaderboard entry then disappear immediately. We record each actual grant or withdrawal with a database timestamp and notice version so the choice can be demonstrated and respected. The casual leaderboard is based on client-submitted progress and is not a verified competition.

5.title: Processors and international transfers
5.body: Cloudflare proxies the sqlheist.com domain and may process request/security data; Vercel serves the static site; Supabase provides authentication and database services for optional accounts; Microsoft Outlook.com/Hotmail handles messages sent to the contact address. The Supabase project database is in its eu-west-1 (Ireland) region. These providers do not receive your local SQL practice payloads from the game.
5.body2: These providers and their disclosed subprocessors may process data outside your country, including outside Türkiye or the EEA. The required transfer mechanisms must be documented for the existing hosting, proxy, and contact-message processing; the corresponding Supabase documentation must be complete before optional accounts are made available. Contact the controller for current provider, subprocessor, transfer-basis, and safeguard details.

6.title: Retention and deletion
6.body: Local data stays until you clear site data. Account, synced progress, and public-profile consent history remain while the account is active; there is currently no automatic inactive-account purge. Public visibility lasts only while you remain opted in. Closed support/privacy correspondence is deleted within 12 months, unless a law or active claim requires longer retention; it is then deleted when that period or claim ends. After we delete a message from Outlook.com, Microsoft says it generally remains in Deleted Items for about 7 days unless emptied sooner and, after that folder is emptied, can remain in Microsoft's systems for up to 30 days before final deletion unless law requires longer.
6.body2: A deletion request immediately makes the profile private, locks later browser writes, and signs you out. The operator permanently deletes the Auth user and cascading profile, progress, and consent-history rows within 30 days. After completion, a private operator-only ledger keeps only a keyed HMAC of the Auth UUID and request, completion, deadline, and confirmation times for at most 90 days, then it is deleted; it contains no email, username, or raw UUID. If provider logs or disaster-recovery copies contain related data, they remain only until no longer needed for security or until the applicable rolling backup is replaced; exact current periods are available from the controller.

7.title: Your rights
7.body: Depending on the law that applies to you, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, and portability, and may withdraw public-profile consent at any time. Account settings provide a JSON export of your email, profile, synced progress, and public-profile consent history, plus visibility and deletion controls.
7.body2: Email melih.sarac@hotmail.com for a request the app cannot complete, including a username correction. We may verify your identity and will respond within the applicable legal deadline. You may also complain to your competent data-protection authority, including Türkiye's Personal Data Protection Authority where applicable.

8.title: Storage, tracking, and security
8.body: This build includes no third-party analytics, advertising trackers, or marketing cookies. It uses browser local storage for language, local progress, this notice, and—only when you sign in—the necessary Supabase session. During signup, the pending email is usable for confirmation/resend for one hour; an expired or malformed entry is removed the next time SQL Heist loads or checks it, and sign-in, sign-out, or clearing site data removes it sooner. Supabase Row Level Security limits base account rows to their owner, but no online system can promise absolute security.

9.title: Children and changes
9.body: SQL Heist is an educational tool aimed at developers and is not directed at children. If you are below the age required to manage an online account where you live, do not create one without a parent or guardian. We will revise this notice and the date above before materially changing these practices. Questions or requests?

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.lead: Play the game, learn the trade, keep it clean. The details:
terms.shortBody: A free, educational game with optional accounts. Use what it teaches only on systems you own or are authorised to test — everything else is your responsibility.

0.title: The deal
0.body: We operate SQL Heist as a free, educational game about how SQL injection works and how to defend against it. By using it, you agree to these terms. If you don't, don't use it.

1.title: Acceptable use
1.body: The techniques here are taught for defensive understanding. You agree to use them only against systems you own or have explicit, documented permission to test. Attacking systems without authorisation is illegal in most places, and you alone are responsible for what you do with what you learn.
1.body2: Don't try to abuse, overload, or reverse the game itself to reach anything other than the practice content it ships with.

2.title: Accounts
2.body: An account is optional. If you create one, provide an email you control, choose a permitted username, protect your credentials, and tell us promptly if you suspect unauthorised access. You are responsible for activity under your session unless applicable law says otherwise.
2.body2: You may export your account data and request deletion from account settings. A request hides and locks the account immediately; permanent deletion is completed manually within 30 days. Our Privacy notice explains the related data processing.

3.title: Public participation
3.body: Public profiles and the casual leaderboard are opt-in. If you join, the public fields described in the Privacy notice can be seen by anyone until you opt out. Do not use a username or display name to impersonate, harass, or publish unlawful content.
3.body2: Leaderboard progress is submitted by browser clients and can be inaccurate or manipulated. It is for informal learning only: no prize, employment decision, security certification, or verified competitive result depends on it.

4.title: Availability and enforcement
4.body: We may change, pause, or discontinue features, and may restrict an account when reasonably necessary for security, abuse prevention, legal compliance, or protection of other users. We will not use this clause to remove rights that applicable law makes mandatory.

5.title: No warranty
5.body: The game and its content are provided “as is,” without warranties of any kind. It's a teaching tool, not professional security advice, and we don't promise it is error-free or fit for any particular purpose. Real systems are more complicated than a practice target.

6.title: Limitation of liability
6.body: To the fullest extent allowed by law, we are not liable for damages arising from your use of the game or the skills it teaches.

7.title: Content
7.body: The game's writing, characters, art, and code are owned by the operator unless noted otherwise. SQL is SQL — the language and the concepts belong to everyone. Don't repackage the game as your own.
7.body2: The “Cowled” mark is by Lorc (https://game-icons.net/1x1/lorc/cowled.html), used under CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/); SQL Heist changes its colour and size.

8.title: Changes
8.body: We may update these terms; when we do, we'll revise the date above. Continuing to play after a change means you accept it. Questions?
